tagline: Home of langsat fruit, Sirikit Dam, and the legendary town of Laplae
introHtml: Uttaradit sits on the seam between the North and the central plains, and plenty of people drive straight through it on the way to Phrae or Nan without stopping. That's a shame, because there's a lot to see. The province is famous for sweet langsat and longkong that come out in the rainy season, and Sirikit Dam holds back the Nan River to form a wide reservoir. Two long-revered shrines, Phra Thaen Sila At and the standing Buddha, are the town's spiritual anchors. Over in Laplae district you'll find a legendary old town with wooden houses, orchards of long-laplae and lin-laplae durian, and the hand-forged knives of Ban Nam Phi, made the old way for generations. If you like quiet towns without the crowds, Uttaradit is easier to enjoy than you'd expect.
bestTime: November–February is cool and pleasant; the rainy season from July–September is when langsat and long-laplae durian come into season

highlights.name: Laplae langsat and longkong
highlights.blurb: The fruit Uttaradit is known for, ripening in the rainy season with sweet, juicy flesh. The town holds a langsat and local-produce festival every year

highlights.name: Sirikit Dam
highlights.blurb: A large earth-fill dam across the Nan River with a broad reservoir, viewpoints, and pretty gardens — a landmark of the province

highlights.name: Laplae town
highlights.blurb: A legendary old district that still has wooden houses, the Laplae town gateway, hillside orchards, and a quiet community life to wander through

highlights.name: Long-laplae and lin-laplae durian
highlights.blurb: Native durian varieties from Laplae — fine, sweet, and creamy with small seeds. They draw people right to the orchards in the rainy season

highlights.name: Ban Nam Phi hand-forged knives
highlights.blurb: The Ban Nam Phi smithing community has made knives and swords from an ancient iron ore source since the days of royal sword-making — a long-standing local craft

highlights.name: Standing Buddha and Phra Thaen Sila At
highlights.blurb: A pair of old temples that locals and visitors alike come to pay respects at, home to both Phra Thaen Sila At and a large standing Buddha

foodScene.name: Khao phan phak
foodScene.note: Steamed rice-flour sheets wrapped around blanched vegetables with broth poured over — a local Laplae breakfast you'll find around the morning market

foodScene.name: Mi phan Laplae
foodScene.note: Rice noodles wrapped with vegetables and egg into bite-size rolls, dipped in a sweet-and-sour sauce — a well-known Laplae snack

foodScene.name: Northern Thai food
foodScene.note: Khao soi, nam ngiao, kaeng hang le, sai ua, and crispy pork (khaep mu) are easy to find across town — the southern-northern take on the cuisine

foodScene.name: Langsat, longkong, and long-laplae durian
foodScene.note: The province's signature fruit, in season during the rains — buy it fresh at the orchards or roadside stalls at local prices

foodScene.name: Noodles and street food in town
foodScene.note: Around the markets and town streets you'll find noodle shops, rice-and-curry stalls, and snacks to graze on without spending much

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals — DIY grill-and-hotpot — with plenty of spots to choose from at friendly prices

foodScene.name: Cafes in town and by the dam
foodScene.note: In town and around Sirikit Dam there are small cafes for a coffee with water and mountain views

foodScene.name: Thong muan and local souvenirs
foodScene.note: Langsat paste, durian paste, and local sweets make good souvenirs, sold at the markets and shops in town

attractions.name: Sirikit Dam
attractions.blurb: An earth-fill dam across the Nan River with a wide reservoir, viewpoints, flower gardens, and lodging if you want to stay over

attractions.name: Laplae town and the Laplae gateway
attractions.blurb: A legendary old district with its town gateway, wooden houses, and quiet community life — good for a stroll and photos

attractions.name: Wat Phra Thaen Sila At
attractions.blurb: An old temple housing Phra Thaen Sila At, a major place of worship in Uttaradit

attractions.name: Wat Phra Yuen Phutthabat Yukhon
attractions.blurb: An old temple with a large standing Buddha and a pair of Buddha footprints, near Phra Thaen Sila At

attractions.name: Ban Nam Phi
attractions.blurb: A knife-forging community with a museum on the Nam Phi iron ore source — see the old smithing craft and buy hand-forged knives

attractions.name: Phraya Phichai Dap Hak Monument
attractions.blurb: A monument to the town's hero in front of the provincial hall — a central landmark of Uttaradit

attractions.name: Wat Phra Fang Sawangkhaburi Muninat
attractions.blurb: An old temple on the Nan River on the site of the ancient town of Fang, with a historic ordination hall and chedi to see

attractions.name: Mon Laplae hillside orchards
attractions.blurb: Hills and long-laplae durian orchards that open up for views and orchard-fresh fruit during the rainy season
